newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes easier in two-way Hong Kong trade.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes easier in two-way Hong Kong trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed easier on Monday in two-way trading as late selling by overseas funds offset early strength, dealers said.

Bullion ended at US$341.00/50 an ounce, down from New York's $341.50/342.00 close on Friday and Hong Kong's previous close of $343.30/80 on February 5, before the market closed for the Chinese New Year holiday.
"Early bargain-hunting and short-covering boosted gold to a day's high of $342.50/343.00, but funds' sales during the afternoon session depressed gold," said a dealer at a local securities house.
"The sentiment was still on the cautious side of bearish, but the price of gold will hold at $340 support levels in the short term," one dealer said.
Local gold ended at HK$3,158 a tael, down HK$43 from its previous close at HK$3,201 on February 3.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -3.00 from its previous fix at +5.00.
